hero.lede: A reference architecture for bringing plant data from electrical rooms, machine lines and utilities into the Faclon platforms, safely. Every area keeps its own segment, a two-firewall industrial DMZ brokers the data, and upload runs outbound only into the plant owner's own cloud tenancy.

kpis.label: Field to cloud, layered on the Purdue model
South and North, with an industrial DMZ between
No write path from IT or cloud to any controller

key_points: One switch, fibre patch panel (LIU) and fibre run per electrical room, machine line and utility section, in a star to a common termination. All electrical rooms share one VLAN with no NAT.
Machine lines keep their existing PLC, DCS and OPC server addressing; overlapping subnets are resolved by 1:1 NAT.
Protocol converters only where a device speaks a non-TCP protocol (Profibus, Modbus RTU and similar) or Profinet cyclic I/O.
South firewall has no default route and accepts nothing inbound from the field. Only I/O Connect and the jump server reach field subnets.
I/O Connect brokers field protocols to HTTPS or MQTT and buffers at least 7 days of data.
Upload is outbound only, over a private link to the plant owner's tenancy. The cloud never initiates a session into the plant.
UDF is the system of record; enterprise apps and AI agents pull data through its API or the Bruce MCP Gateway.
Firewall and master-switch HA pairs are optional.

platforms.name: I/O Connect
platforms.role: Pipeline gateway for plant data across many OT protocols
platforms.notes: Polls field devices read-only, brokers them to HTTPS 443 or MQTT/TLS 8883, buffers at least 7 days and replays in order. Holds field credentials locally. Can also sit on the OT or IT network where a design calls for it.

platforms.name: UDF
platforms.role: Unified Data Fabric: ingestion, system of record and data API
platforms.notes: Private ingestion endpoint with mutual TLS per gateway and idempotent writes, so buffered data replays without duplicates. Time-series, document, graph and vector storage with retention and downsampling per tag class. Read-only, OAuth2 API per consumer with rate limits and an audit log of every call. Not exposed outside the platform. An edge instance in the DMZ is optional.

platforms.name: I/O Sense
platforms.notes: Default visualisation apps for plant and corporate users on web and mobile, with App Studio for new apps. Access by plant, area and app through Foundry.

platforms.name: Foundry
platforms.role: Governance: authentication, users and access across all platforms
platforms.notes: Single sign-on with the customer's identity provider; role-based access by plant, area and app; per-consumer API clients; audit trail into the customer SIEM.

platforms.name: Forge
platforms.role: Deployment layer inside the customer's tenancy
platforms.notes: Spins up and manages the platform's compute, containers and libraries on any public cloud or on-premise, inside a private network with no public IPs.

platforms.name: Ontology
platforms.role: Asset model and directory of what exists and how it is served
platforms.notes: ISA-95 style site → area → line → asset hierarchy; units, ranges and descriptions for every tag, used by I/O Sense, Bruce and API consumers.

platforms.name: Bruce
platforms.role: Agent factory, plus the Bruce MCP Gateway for agentic data access
platforms.notes: Needs a model token and API access. Preferred: a model endpoint inside the customer's own tenancy so data does not leave it. Read-only MCP tools, per-user or per-agent auth through Foundry, prompts and responses logged; no write tools.

platforms.name: Deepsense
platforms.role: Build, deploy and run custom ML and AI models
platforms.notes: Runs on platform compute, reads from UDF and writes results back as derived tags. An edge instance in the DMZ is optional for local inference; it reads from I/O Connect and has no route to field subnets.

flows.d: Non-TCP devices are polled through their converter; PLCs and DCS controllers are read over CIP explicit messaging or through their OPC server; boiler and turbine DCS are read through their OPC server.
On any break, I/O Connect keeps polling and buffers locally, then replays in order when the link returns.
Consumers only pull. Nothing in IT or the cloud can reach I/O Connect or any field device.
S5 stays disabled until an access window is approved; vendor accounts are time-bound.
IT access to the manager is blocked by N8. Sealed local break-glass accounts cover a manager outage.

design_rules: Star, one area per run

Every electrical room, machine line and utility section has its own switch, LIU and fibre run to the common termination, so one cut affects one area only. Machine lines and utility sections are each their own subnet behind a NAT switch.
One VLAN for electrical rooms

Meters and converters are of one type and trust level and are addressed fresh by the project, so one VLAN means one South FW sub-interface and one rule instead of one per room. A few hundred devices is far below any broadcast concern; if room count grows large, split it by building.
Lines as cell/area zones
Existing PLC addressing is left unchanged; overlapping OEM subnets (for example 192.168.1.0/24 on several lines) are resolved by 1:1 NAT on the line's NAT-capable industrial switch.
Real-time traffic stays in the cell
EtherNet/IP implicit I/O, Profinet RT, drive and safety networks stay inside each cell and are never translated or routed.
Converters only where needed

Added only where data is not reachable over a routable TCP protocol: serial and fieldbus links (Modbus RTU on RS-485, Profibus DP) and Profinet cyclic I/O. A gateway configured as a Profinet I/O device exposes it as Modbus TCP or OPC UA. Where the PLC supports native Ethernet reads (S7 or OPC UA), reading it directly usually avoids the gateway.
Read-only acquisition
No write path exists from the IDMZ, IT or cloud to any PLC or controller.
Routes held by two hosts only
The South FW has no default route and no static routes; only I/O Connect and the jump server hold routes to field subnets. The North FW has no route to field subnets at all.
A broker, not a pass-through
I/O Connect terminates field protocols and re-originates HTTPS / MQTT to UDF: two sessions, never one. It holds field credentials locally.
Outbound only
The cloud never initiates a session into the plant. All data movement from plant to cloud is outbound from the IDMZ.
Firewalls are the only way between segments
The IDMZ switch is Layer 2 with no SVI in any VLAN. The firewall manager is the only source allowed to change either OT firewall, and it is reached only from the jump server.
Locked-down trunks
Trunks carry an explicit allowed-VLAN list, native VLAN 999 with no ports, negotiation disabled. VLAN 1 is not used.
considerations: Private connectivity to the cloud tenancy (site-to-site IPsec or a dedicated cloud interconnect)
Keeps plant data off the public internet and lets the perimeter rule be scoped to tenancy prefixes
Recommended
Store-and-forward on I/O Connect, sized for at least 7 days
Covers WAN outages and planned firewall maintenance without data loss
Recommended
NTP across converters, I/O Connect and firewalls (VLAN 14)
Energy meters often have no reliable clock; timestamps must be consistent before they reach UDF
Recommended
Converter list per device: Profibus, Profinet I/O, Modbus RTU, and on older lines DeviceNet or ControlNet
Decides how many converters are needed; devices already on EtherNet/IP, Modbus TCP or OPC UA need none. Profibus and Profinet gateways also need a change to the master PLC's hardware configuration
Site survey
Electrical rooms on one shared VLAN, no NAT; NAT only where OEM devices have fixed or overlapping IPs
Converters are newly addressed by the project, so a managed L2 switch per room is enough. Saves NAT switches and firewall sub-interfaces
